summary: MemoryMark bridge is a single flat FastAPI module (bridge/server.py) under uv/Python 3.12. Single existing _lifespan hooks startup/teardown. No streaming endpoints or background tasks yet. WAL path is exposed at mempalace.mcp_server._WAL_FILE; tests monkeypatch it via autouse fixture.

key_facts.module_layout: single flat bridge/server.py (no src/ or package split)
claude_md_rules: use uv as python package manager
always use uv when running python
key_facts.wal_access_via_bridge: server.py already imports `import mempalace.mcp_server as _mp` and reads _mp._wal_log, _mp._metadata_cache — private-attr access across module boundary is an established pattern
key_facts.wal_redirect_in_tests: bridge/conftest.py autouse fixture `isolated_palace` monkeypatches _mp._WAL_DIR and _mp._WAL_FILE to tmp_path; read at call time, not captured at import time
key_facts.route_handler_style: sync def (not async); only MCP handlers and _lifespan are async

wal_format.on_disk_format: JSON lines, one object per line; mode 0o600; O_APPEND|O_CREAT
wal_format.guarantees: append-only, readable concurrently, no sequence IDs written, line number is a safe monotonic ID

write_paths_emitting_wal_entries: mempalace.mcp_server.tool_delete_drawer (line 577) — called by REST DELETE and MCP

reusable_patterns.pattern: asyncio.to_thread for sync I/O from async context
monkeypatch WAL path in autouse fixture
TestClient streaming: `with client.stream('GET', url) as r: for line in r.iter_lines(): ...`
reusable_patterns.source: not yet used; supported by httpx

test_conventions.async_tests: none; use synchronous TestClient even for async routes
test_conventions.assertion_style: assert resp.status_code == N; assert data['success'] is True

architecture_notes.new_file_policy: No precedent for second module — both inline in server.py and new bridge/events.py are acceptable. Given scope (tailer + registry + endpoint), a new bridge/events.py improves readability without violating any rule.
architecture_notes.dependency_strategy: sse_starlette is already installed but undeclared. Plain starlette.responses.StreamingResponse is sufficient (ships with fastapi) and avoids declaring a new dep. Prefer it for minimal footprint.
architecture_notes.background_task: Start the WAL tailer as asyncio.create_task inside _lifespan; store task handle in a module-level global; cancel+await on lifespan exit.
